overview: Medieval India - Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara, Mughals (with Marathas, Qutb Shahis, successor states), Bhakti and Sufism: 57 official questions (2008-2024), the largest A-block section; Mughal political history alone has 18. 41 are one-liners (who built/founded/introduced, which rate, which reign); since 2023 each paper carries 3-5 matching items (authors-works, officials-duties, travellers-reigns).

possibility.what_they_ask: who built/did X (Quwwat-ul-Islam, market control); founding year of Bahmani; why Ghori won; post system
coins (tanka, jital); taxes (khams); canals; music; author-work and traveller-country matching
rivals (Bahmani), Talikota 1565, siege defence, Aravidu rulers and Jesuits
which king abolished marriage tax; literary courts; women authors; foreign visitor-reign pairs; temple-place pairs

possibility.angle: Mughal political history and administration (with Marathas, Jats, Qutb Shahis, successor states)
possibility.what_they_ask: founder and decisive battles; childhood names; Sher Shah revenue and roads; events of a reign; revenue officials; Later Mughal order; Ashtapradhan posts; successor-state founders
monument-place; buildings of a reign (Akbar); historians' books; Sikh Gurus; music styles
saint-doctrine (Advaita, Pushtimarga); saint-region; Bhakti-Sufi common ideas; 18th-c. poets' languages
saint titles (Garib Nawaz); which silsila a saint belongs to

traps.trap: [Builder vs completer] Monument given to the king who extended it
traps.spot: Delhi monuments with Aibak, Iltutmish, Alauddin all offered
traps.fix: Quwwat-ul-Islam built by Aibak; Iltutmish completed Qutb Minar; Alauddin = Alai Darwaza
Alauddin 1/2; Sher Shah 1/3 of average produce; Akbar's zabt about 1/3
traps.pyq: '1/4 of the produce was collected' → 1/3 [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#16]; rate under Sher Shah → 1/3 [group1-prelims-2012#83]

traps.trap: Foreign visitor placed in the wrong kingdom or reign
traps.spot: Visitor-reign pairs with Razzaq, Paes, Nuniz, Nikitin, Conti
traps.fix: Nikitin visited the Bahmani kingdom; Razzaq 1443 = Devaraya II; Paes = Krishnadevaraya; Frederick 1567

traps.trap: Later event pulled into a reign
traps.fix: Kandahar was lost (1622) under Jahangir, not annexed; Arjan Dev 1606, Mewar 1615, Hawkins 1608 are his

traps.trap: Battle that founded vs battle that secured
traps.spot: Panipat I, Khanwa, Panipat II, Kannauj together
traps.fix: Panipat 1526 = foundation; Khanwa 1527 = real beginning/expansion; Kannauj 1540 = Humayun's loss

traps.spot: Qutb Shahi options Ibrahim / Muhammad Quli / Muhammad / Abdullah
traps.fix: Hyderabad (Bhagyanagar) 1591 = Muhammad Quli; Hussain Sagar = Ibrahim

traps.trap: Shared feature claimed where they differ
traps.spot: 'Common to Bhakti and Sufi' list including idol worship
traps.fix: Both rejected idol worship; shared monotheism, simple living, tolerance
traps.pyq: 'Accepted idol worship to some extent' → excluded [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#14]

traps.trap: Poet's language swapped with a neighbouring region
traps.fix: Dayaram = Gujarati; Waris Shah = Punjabi; Kunchan Nambiar = Malayalam; Tayumanavar = Tamil

techniques.name: Reign timeline slotting
techniques.how: [Event → year → reign] Put a year on every event in a 'which happened under X' list; keep only those inside the reign's dates.
techniques.example: Jahangir 1605-27: Arjan Dev 1606, EIC 1608, Mewar 1615 fit; Kandahar was lost 1622 not annexed → 'I, II and IV only' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#17]

techniques.name: Order by succession anchors
techniques.how: For later Mughals, fix the first two and the long reign (Muhammad Shah 1719-48); the right code has Farrukhsiyar before Muhammad Shah.
techniques.example: Bahadur Shah > Jahandar > Farrukhsiyar > Muhammad Shah > Shah Alam II; the other codes misplace Farrukhsiyar [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#20]

techniques.name: Author-work by period
techniques.how: Place each author in a century and patron; the work's title often names the patron (Nasiri, Firoz Shahi).
techniques.example: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri → Minhaj (Nasiruddin's reign); Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi → Barani; Tahqiq-i-Hind → Al-Biruni; Rihla → Battuta [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#28]

techniques.name: Policy fingerprint
techniques.how: Each Sultan has a fixed set of measures; read the cluster in the stem and match it to one Sultan.
techniques.example: Liquor ban + market control + harsh punishments → Alauddin Khalji, not Firuz (welfare) or Iltutmish (coins) [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#4]

techniques.name: Court-name lookup
techniques.how: Vijayanagara literary halls map one-to-one to kings; eliminate by dynasty phase (Sangama vs Tuluva).
techniques.example: Mutyalasala → Devaraya II (Sangama); Bhuvanavijayam is Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva) [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#93]

techniques.name: Doctrine-founder table
techniques.how: Keep the Vedanta/Bhakti table: Sankara Advaita, Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita, Madhva Dvaita, Nimbarka Dvaitadvaita, Vallabha Suddhadvaita/Pushtimarga.
techniques.example: Pushtimarga → Vallabhacharya; Chaitanya is Gaudiya, Vyasaraja is Dvaita [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#20]

confusions.remember: foundation vs real beginning and expansion (Rana Sanga)
Prithviraj won I; Ghori won II with mounted archers
aunt married Jahangir 1611 vs niece married Shah Jahan
tanka, jital, iqta vs market control, dagh, huliya
Persian at Vijayanagara 1443 vs Russian at Bahmani 1469-74
Kampana's wife on Madurai vs Telugu Ramayana / Varadambika Parinayam
Moinuddin, Nizamuddin, Gesudaraz vs Bahauddin Zakariya, Sadruddin Arif
Sikandara vs Delhi (built in Akbar's reign)
foreign affairs, ceremonies vs intelligence-household / correspondence

anchors: 1192 Tarain II; 1206 Slave dynasty; 1336 Vijayanagara; 1347 Bahmani (Gulbarga)
1526 Panipat I; 1527 Khanwa; 1540 Kannauj; 1556 Panipat II, Akbar crowned at Kalanaur
Sher Shah: uniform measurement, 3 land classes, 1/3 share; Sonargaon-Indus road
Iltutmish: silver tanka, copper jital; khams = 1/5 of booty to state
Abdur Razzaq 1443 (Devaraya II); Venkatapati Raya II allowed Jesuit churches at Chandragiri and Nellore
Jahangir: 1606 Arjan Dev, 1611 Nur Jahan, 1615 Mewar, 1622 Kandahar lost
Later Mughals: Bahadur Shah I - Jahandar - Farrukhsiyar - Muhammad Shah (1719-48) - Shah Alam II
Shivaji: Torna first fort (c.1646); guru Ramdas; Raigad coronation 1674
Successor states: Murshid Quli (Bengal), Chin Qilich Khan (Hyderabad), Safdar Jung (Awadh)
checklist: Built, completed or extended? Name the original builder.
Put a year on each event and test it against the reign.
Fractions in revenue questions: match ruler to his fixed rate.
Visitor questions: which kingdom did he actually visit, and in which reign?
In matching, start with the pair whose title names the patron (Nasiri, Firoz Shahi).
Same-dynasty name lists: recall the one deed each ruler is known for.
